items: Stress has plateaued rather than accelerated, and the debate has moved from redemptions to refinancing. S&P’s credit-estimate default rate fell to 3.93% in June from 4.79% in March and direct lending defaults are below 4% for the first time in more than three years; Fitch’s broader measure is flat at about 6% (6.2% in October). BDC non-accruals of 2.87% are a five-year high but concentrated in a few names.

The software wall has been pushed out, not taken down. Software direct loans due in 2026–27 fell from 8.4% to 5.7% of the total, but loans with under three years to run reached a series-high 32%. Realised software defaults are only 1.2% against 6.0% overall, yet Barclays finds 2028 software maturities marked at $89.4 against $92.8 for other sectors.

Defaults are mostly restructurings; the loss rate is the number that matters. S&P counts 125 distressed exchanges against 29 conventional defaults over twelve months. Morgan Stanley keeps its 8% default forecast through mid-2027 but, with 70–80% recoveries, translates it into credit losses of 1.6–2.4%.

Pricing has turned in lenders’ favour while volume shrinks. The unitranche spread widened to 522bp in July from a 490bp trough, a 91bp premium over single-B loans, while origination of US$120bn to July is down 23%. The risk is that record fundraising (US$129.15bn in nine months) competes the improvement away.

No warning signals across our three funds, on marks that predate the third quarter. All are valued as of 30 June 2026. PAG’s net IRR is 14.2% with DPI of 0.38x; Guggenheim holds 18% software against about 30% for large BDCs, with 2 names on its monitor list; every HSBC facility is rated Green.

Global private debt AUM is US$2,548.6bn (institutional 75.7%). Institutional AUM fell by US$91.2bn in 2025, the first annual decline in the series, while retail and insurance grew to US$413.2bn and US$206.8bn; BDC assets are US$576bn.

Supply: dry powder fell to US$547.0bn (39.6% of NAV, the lowest in the series) from US$669.2bn. Funds raised US$157.7bn across 89 vehicles in 1H26 after US$264.8bn across 292 in 2025 — fewer, larger funds.

Demand: refinancing volume is down 47% but LBO financing is up 4%. Private credit financed 72% of 2Q26 LBOs by count, the first quarter below 80% since 3Q24. Middle-market CLO issuance of US$17.77bn in 1H26 is up 5.2% while BSL CLO issuance fell 26.2%.

Returns: private debt returned 7.8% a year from 2015 to June 2026 with 2.1% volatility, but marks are smoothed and correlation with syndicated loans is 82.4%. The twelve-month return is 8.3% against 4.4% for single-B loans; yields are 10.3% against 8.3%.
Pricing and terms: new deals price at 500–550bp. Documentation is weakest at the top: only 26% of 2024-vintage upper middle-market deals carry a financial covenant and 41% have a PIK toggle.

rows: Stress is contained and concentrated; 8% defaults through mid-2027 but 1.6–2.4% losses; software refinancing risk is building.
Volume US$166bn YTD, down 35%; spreads at 500–550bp; 269 issuers on its default risk radar; liquidity ample.
Rates volatility is the swing factor; fundamental improvement stalls; 7% of the loan index trades below $80.
Focus shifts to the asset side: software marked at $93.1 on average; BDC spreads do not look cheap.
About 21% of private credit debt matures within two years; defaults seen at 7–8% by end-2027; refinancing may itself trigger deterioration.

items: PAG BRS III: subscription line finance is 60% of the book; two new SME investments; net IRR eased from 14.7% and DPI rose from 0.30x. The largest bank counterparty rose to 25% of invested amount from 17%.
Guggenheim PDF IV: five deals closed in the quarter; year-to-date closings at S+539, 4.2x first-lien net leverage and 42% loan-to-value; PIK under 2% of income; AtHome added to the monitor list.
HSBC RCF: fund size EUR 434.8m after EUR 100m of new commitments; three facilities added; average utilisation 10.6%.
Ask Guggenheim for the maturity profile of its software loans by year, detail on the two monitor-list names, and fund-level return figures.
Raise counterparty concentration with PAG and ask how it will be managed as the investment period ends in December 2026.
In every manager review, ask for the number of loans amended, extended or switched to PIK and the marks applied, not only for defaults.
Treat HSBC’s utilisation rate as its early-warning indicator and track it quarterly.
Whether Fitch’s default rate holds its plateau near 6% and S&P’s stays below 4%.
Software refinancing: the share of loans with under three years to run (32%) and the marks on 2028 maturities.
Whether spread widening survives record fundraising and third-quarter volume that fell 28% year on year.
Policy and rates: the Labor Department’s safe-harbour rule, the SEC’s interval-fund proposal and the path of base rates.
